proposals.before: During palace games Wu Di pointed out the boy to the witless Hui: 'That one is your heir.'
proposals.after: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, [Emperor Wu] took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents "witless" and renders 兒 as "heir"; Chinese and literal say the emperor took the princes' hands and called Yu Hui's son.

proposals.before: Pan Yue forged spirit-prayer lines; drunk Yu copied them under Chen Wu's orders.
proposals.after: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the crown prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having small maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic wrongly attributes the copying orders to Chen Wu; Chinese assigns the paper and draft to maid Chengfu (承福).

proposals.before: An imperial train stripped Yu at Eastern Palace.
proposals.after: Thereupon Minister Director He Yu was dispatched with insignia, Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Prince of Liang Tong, Eastern Garrison General Prince of Huainan Yun, Forward General Eastern Martial Duke Dan, Prince of Zhao Lun, and Grand Tutor He Shao to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as commoner.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic over-compresses and drops named envoys present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Verses mocked Empress Nanfeng and Yu's childhood name.'
proposals.after: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'
proposals.reason: Idiomatic is truncated commentary rather than translating the rhyme; trailing quote mark is corrupt.

proposals.after: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
proposals.reason: Chinese 沙門 is Shamen; "White Sand" confuses the rhyme's 白沙 with the childhood name.

proposals.before: 'White Sand' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
proposals.after: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
proposals.reason: Literal also mistranslates 沙門 as White Sand.

proposals.before: After Lady Xie's mother died no one comforted him.
proposals.after: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic replaces first-person letter voice and mistranslates 宜城君 as "Xuan city"; also this unit is Yu's letter, not narrator summary.

proposals.before: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi Ce to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
proposals.after: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
proposals.reason: 伊 is the envoy's name; 策 is the investiture/announcement verb, not part of a personal name Yi Ce.

decisions.after: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'
decisions.reason: Before invents "witless" and mistranslates 兒 as "heir," but the proposal wrongly makes Emperor Wu take the princes' hands; after 惠帝來朝 the hand-taking continues Hui's greeting, and 惠帝乃止 confirms he stopped that greeting when Wu said 是汝兒也.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」

decisions.after: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.
decisions.reason: Before wrongly credits Chen Wu with ordering the copy; Chinese has Pan Yue draft the prayer-like text and 小婢承福 deliver paper, brush, and draft so the drunken Crown Prince writes it. The revision preserves his established title and renders 小婢 naturally.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之

decisions.after: Thereupon Minister Director He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Tong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Eastern Martial Duke; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Tutor He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the Crown Prince as a commoner.
decisions.reason: Before collapses the deposition embassy into a nameless "imperial train"; Chinese names 尚書和郁, 解結, 梁王肜, 淮南王允, 東武公澹, 趙王倫, and 太保何劭. The revision restores every envoy using their established full names and titles and makes the long list legible in English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 使尚書和郁持節，解結為副，及大將軍梁王肜、鎮東將軍淮南王允、前將軍東武公澹、趙王倫、太保何劭詣東宮

decisions.reason: Before replaces the rhyme with truncated commentary and a stray quote mark; Chinese quotes the full children's verse 南風起兮吹白沙…, which the proposed rendering restores.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又曰：「南風起兮吹白沙，遙望魯國郁嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。」

decisions.reason: 沙門 is the childhood byname Shamen; "White Sand" confuses it with 白沙 in the preceding rhyme, and the proposed "Shamen" restores the gloss.
The literal likewise misrenders 沙門 as "White Sand"; replacing it with "Shamen" matches the childhood byname in the Chinese gloss.
This sentence is still Yu's first-person letter; before shifts to third person and paraphrases away the title 宜城君, while the proposed wording keeps 自宜城君亡 and 不見存恤 in first person.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 自宜城君亡，不見存恤，恆在空室中坐。

decisions.reason: In the patent formula 衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈, 伊 is the envoy's name and 策 the announcement verb; treating "Yi Ce" as a personal name is wrong, and the proposed wording restores that parse.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰
